events.title: Opera Mini pilot launched
events.summary: Opera introduced Opera Mini on August 10, 2005 as a TV 2 Norway pilot — a proxy-based mobile browser; worldwide launch followed on January 24, 2006.
events.about: Opera Mini brought the web to billions of low-end phones long before smartphones were common: pages were rendered remotely, shrunk, and sent as images or simplified markup. It was how many users in emerging markets first experienced email, news, and search on a phone.

narrative.whyChosen: Opera Mini pioneered mobile web access before the iPhone era.
narrative.whyImportant: Server-side compression made browsing usable on 2G networks and tiny screens worldwide.
narrative.problemSolved: Feature phones lacked the [CPU] and bandwidth to run full desktop browsers locally.

events.title: Puppet first released
events.summary: Luke Kanies released Puppet in August 2005 — a declarative configuration management tool for automating server state.
events.about: Puppet describes desired system state in a domain-specific language — installed packages, file permissions, running services — and enforces it on agents. Enterprises used it to manage thousands of nodes before Ansible and cloud-native tooling. Example: declare `nginx` installed and a config file templated from a central catalog.

narrative.whyChosen: Puppet pioneered idempotent, model-driven infrastructure [automation] for production fleets.
narrative.whyImportant: It proved declarative config management could scale beyond shell scripts and CFEngine.
narrative.problemSolved: Sysadmins could not keep hundreds of servers consistent by hand or with ad-hoc scripts.
